instructions: Right now our application is relying on email notifications (cloudflare worker) and supabase is logging these emails and parsing out info along with using a guthub function to pull data from GO to get trips ids. This is all working properly now. The good news is GO Transit gave me an API key: 30029868 and attached documentation on how to use it and what is available to colect. This is a big change so I would like open a new branch to not affect my current working version using emails. I should also create new tables in supabase to collect the data from API calls and not emails if this makes sense .

plan.goal: Introduce a dedicated GO Transit Open API ingestion pipeline and new Supabase tables on an isolated branch while keeping the existing email-driven pipeline operational.
assumptions: The Metrolinx Open API base URL is 'https://api.openmetrolinx.com/OpenDataAPI/api/V1' accepting the API key via query parameter 'key=30029868'.
Ingestion will focus on ServiceUpdates (delays and alerts) and TripUpdates (real-time train delay status and trip identifiers) for the Barrie line.
New Supabase tables ('go_api_service_alerts', 'go_api_trip_updates') will be created with anon read RLS policies and service-role write access, leaving 'go_train_delays' intact.
A Python-based scheduled GitHub Action runner will ingest the API payloads into Supabase on a regular schedule, mirroring the project's existing GTFS refresh patterns.

phases.name: Database Schema for API Ingestion
phases.goal: Create SQL migration defining dedicated Supabase tables, indexes, and RLS policies for Metrolinx API alerts and trip updates.
changes: Define 'go_api_service_alerts' table storing alert metadata (alert_id, service_date, line_code, delay_minutes, status, message, raw_json, received_at).
Define 'go_api_trip_updates' table storing trip real-time updates (trip_id, line_code, direction_code, delay_seconds, schedule_relationship, stop_time_updates, updated_at).
Add indexes on service_date, line_code, received_at, and trip_id.
Add Row Level Security (RLS) policies allowing public read (anon key) and full write/update access to service_role.
verification: SQL migration executes without syntax errors in Supabase SQL editor.
Tables are visible in Supabase with RLS enabled allowing SELECT for public/anon and blocking unauthenticated INSERT/UPDATE.

phases.name: GO Transit API Ingestion Script and Workflow
phases.goal: Build an ingestion script and scheduled GitHub Action to poll Metrolinx Open API endpoints and persist delay updates into Supabase.
changes: Create 'scripts/ingest_go_api.py' using requests and Supabase client to query Metrolinx API endpoints ('ServiceUpdate/ServiceAlert/All' and 'ServiceUpdate/TripUpdates') with API key '30029868' (configurable via METROLINX_API_KEY).
Implement Barrie Line filtering ('BR' line / corridor), Toronto timezone normalization for service dates, and idempotent upserts into 'go_api_service_alerts' and 'go_api_trip_updates'.
Create '.github/workflows/ingest_go_api.yml' scheduled to run every 5-10 minutes with manual workflow_dispatch support using repository secrets SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY.
verification: Running 'python scripts/ingest_go_api.py' locally or via workflow_dispatch fetches data from Metrolinx and successfully populates rows in 'go_api_service_alerts' and 'go_api_trip_updates'.
Re-running the script does not create duplicate entries for the same alert or trip update timestamp.

phases.name: Frontend Data Source Compatibility Layer
phases.goal: Expose an optional environment-driven switch in Supabase data client to allow querying the new API data source while preserving fallback to email delay tables.
changes: Update 'src/lib/supabase.js' to export TABLE configurable via 'VITE_DELAY_DATA_SOURCE' ('api' -> 'go_api_service_alerts', default -> 'go_train_delays').
Add adapter mapper in 'src/lib/supabase.js' to map API table fields to the dashboard's expected alert schema (line, direction, delay_minutes, status, message, service_date).
verification: Dashboard runs and loads existing data from 'go_train_delays' by default.
When 'VITE_DELAY_DATA_SOURCE=api' is configured, dashboard fetches and displays delay entries from 'go_api_service_alerts' without console errors or visual regressions.
